entry_point.discipline_context: Design variables such as thicknesses, angles, and material parameters are adjusted to reduce a scalar performance objective.
entry_point.rationale: Mechanical design gives a concrete reason to move through a multidimensional parameter space while retaining the general mathematics.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: Design language is an intuition for the mathematics, not an additional optimisation theorem or engineering guarantee.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: Exact line search is explicitly requested.
Its quadratic convergence scope explains the requested Heavy Ball method.
Its convergence result is required with Nesterov acceleration.
The stochastic-gradient assumptions are explicitly requested.
The stochastic-gradient update and error-floor implication are in scope.
Step-size conditions for stochastic gradients are explicitly requested.
Newton's method requires its second-order model.
Newton's update and implementation semantics are explicitly requested.
Newton convergence scope is relevant to comparison.
The BFGS update and curvature condition are explicitly requested.

chapter_sequence.title: From design objective to optimality
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce unconstrained objectives and first- and second-order tests.

chapter_sequence.title: Geometry of smooth and convex objectives
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build smoothness, convexity, strong convexity, Hessian bounds, and conditioning.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and choosing a step
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the update, constant steps, exact line search, and Armijo backtracking.

chapter_sequence.title: Rates and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: State convex and strongly convex rates and distinguish Heavy Ball from Nesterov acceleration.

chapter_sequence.title: Noisy gradients and adaptive steps
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present stochastic assumptions, step-size conditions, and adaptive gradient algorithms.

chapter_sequence.title: Curvature-aware methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect Newton and BFGS to local curvature and numerical linear algebra.

chapter_sequence.title: Turning updates into Python
chapter_sequence.purpose: Make the mathematical state, gradient, step, and diagnostics explicit in implementation.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate theorem scope, one update calculation, and code diagnosis.

implementation_strategy: Use NumPy-style arrays, explicit current-iterate gradients, stable linear solves, and printed intermediate values so code mirrors the equations.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three final worked exercises: a theorem-scope check, a unified gradient-update calculation, and a buggy-versus-corrected Python diagnosis.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify which assumptions justify stationarity, a convex rate, and local Newton convergence.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Interpret claims about an optimisation routine used in a mechanical design study.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Differentiate a two-variable objective and perform one positive-step gradient update.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Treat the two coordinates as design variables in a small surrogate objective.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Diagnose a stale-gradient and sign error, then match corrected Python output to one gradient step.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Inspect a short design-optimisation script before trusting its reported parameter update.
